news.headline: Fagnano off injury report, set to start for Ravens vs. Jaguars
news.detail: Rookie Joe Fagnano (ankle) came off the Ravens' injury report on Nov 4 and starts in place of the injured Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley. Kicker Tyler Loop is on IR. Jaguars DE Travon Walker (ribs) was limited Tuesday.

news.headline: 49ers missing McCaffrey, Evans and Samuel at Wednesday practice
news.detail: On Nov 4 the 49ers had Christian McCaffrey (hamstring), Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel sidelined. Nick Bosa returned to practice. Brock Purdy is healthy. Early-week listings can change by Friday.

news.headline: Mahomes full at practice; Jets WR Garrett Wilson sat out Wednesday
news.detail: Patrick Mahomes (knee) was a full participant Nov 4. The Jets were without Garrett Wilson in practice. Travis Kelce and Rashee Rice were limited.

news.headline: Seahawks: Darnold out, Lock is the QB; Smith-Njigba listed as rest day
news.detail: Mike Macdonald said Sam Darnold won't play Sunday (quad, ribs). Drew Lock is on the report with a right elbow issue. Jaxon Smith-Njigba's Wednesday listing was a rest day, not an injury. Charles Cross, Leonard Williams and Rashid Shaheed did not practice.

news.headline: Burrow healthy after 462-yard game; Falcons lose Branch and Ebukam for Madrid
news.detail: Joe Burrow went 33 of 48 for 462 yards last week and is healthy. Falcons WR Zachariah Branch and DE Samson Ebukam are out (hamstrings). Bengals defenders DJ Turner, Cedric Johnson and Kyle Dugger missed Wednesday's estimated practice.

news.headline: Eagles start Joe Milton; Barkley, Smith and Wicks missed Wednesday practice
news.detail: Philadelphia is on a six-game losing streak and Jalen Hurts is out for the season. Joe Milton makes his first NFL start over Tanner McKee. Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks did not practice Nov 4. Giants RB Cam Skattebo and edge Abdul Carter also sat out.

news.headline: Rams QB Stafford questionable with arm soreness; Adams on IR
news.detail: Matthew Stafford was listed questionable early in the week with right arm soreness. Davante Adams is on IR, which could raise Puka Nacua's target share. CB Jaylen Watson is out for the season. Jayden Daniels was a full participant for Washington.

news.headline: Lions' St. Brown limited with rib injury; center Mays unlikely to play
news.detail: Amon-Ra St. Brown (rib) was limited Wednesday in an estimated walkthrough report. Jahmyr Gibbs is off the injury report. Center Cade Mays hurt his ankle and Dan Campbell doesn't expect him to play. LB Jack Campbell is out after a neck injury.

NFL.recap: Week 8 went well against the spread (9-5) and the winner picks were 11 of 13 with a pick, but totals were 6-7. The big misses were efficiency or finishing-drive swings: JAX 42, IND 7 (24 points off), CHI 34, SEA 17 (20 off), and PIT over CLE (16 off). Close games were within a touchdown, as in NE-MIA, KC-DEN and GB-CAR. Season winners are 25 of 40 and spread is 18-22-1. Top-pick lists are under their expected hits on winners, value picks and underdogs.

lessons.lesson: When the model picks a different winner than the Vegas favorite, it has mostly lost so far.
lessons.evidence: 2 of 7 graded games where the model's side was not the Vegas favorite won (CIN over BAL and DEN over KC won; PHI over DAL, NYG over NO, ATL over CHI, PHI over CAR, NE over CHI lost). Week 8 added no new cases. This week PHI over NYG (model 51%, Vegas 40%) would be a new case.
lessons.test: On past seasons, take every game where the model's pick differs from the moneyline favorite. Compare its win rate and spread record with Vegas. Wait for 20+ games.

lessons.lesson: Large gaps between the model's total and Vegas's total have not paid off.
lessons.evidence: 0 of 5 graded games with a gap of 4.9 or more won the over/under pick. Smaller gaps are mixed: ARI-DAL at 4.2 lost, BUF-BAL at 3.9 won, CHI-SEA at 3.2 lost, TEN-CIN at 2.5 lost. Overall the over/under is 20-20 (week 8 was 6-7). Two Under picks this week (TB-CHI at 5.0, CIN-ATL at 4.9) will add to the large-gap sample. News for CIN-ATL (Burrow healthy after 462 yards) is not favorable to the Under.
lessons.test: On past seasons, group games by size of the total gap (under 2, 2-4, over 4). Check hit rate per group. Needs 20+ games in the large-gap group.

lessons.lesson: Many big misses come from efficiency swings, which the model can't see before kickoff.
lessons.evidence: In 9 of the 15 games where the winner was wrong, the review names efficiency as the main reason (DAL-PHI, TB-CAR, NYG-HOU, ARI-LA, CHI-ATL, CAR-PHI, BAL-CLE, ARI-DAL, CHI-SEA). Turnovers led in NO-NYG and SF-ATL. MIA-NYJ and NE-CHI were close. HOU-JAX had no clear reason. Week 8 blowouts (JAX-IND, PIT-CLE) were driven by finishing drives.
lessons.test: On past seasons, measure how often big spread misses (over 8 points) are driven by efficiency versus turnovers. Check whether the model's misses are larger than Vegas's overall.

lessons.lesson: Big-game player picks are close to the model's chances on hit rate, but still lose units.
lessons.evidence: 8 of 27 big-game picks hit, against 8.9 expected, at -9.46 units. The earlier hit-rate shortfall has mostly closed. Milestone picks are 22 of 29 against 21.7 expected, at -3.28 units.
lessons.test: On past seasons, compare predicted chance with actual hit rate for long-shot props in buckets of model chance. Also check whether the prices paid are shorter than fair odds. Needs 20+ picks per bucket.

lessons.lesson: Best-value picks against the sportsbook are running below the model's chances.
lessons.evidence: 7 of 17 best-value picks hit this season, against 9.0 expected, at -3.64 units. Several sit only 0.1 to 2 points over break-even this week.
lessons.test: On past seasons, check hit rate of the model's top value picks by size of edge. Needs 20+ picks.

lessons.lesson: The model's margin errors are larger than Vegas's, and it is below .500 against the spread.
lessons.evidence: Average spread miss is 10.1 for the model against 9.3 for Vegas over 41 graded games. The model is 18-22-1 against the spread (9-5 in week 8). Winners are 25 of 40.
lessons.test: On past seasons, compare the model's average absolute margin error with Vegas's, by week, over a full season. Also check ATS record by season. Do this before changing anything.

lessons.lesson: Big gaps between the model and Vegas may come from lineup changes the model hasn't picked up.
lessons.evidence: DAL at PHI listed Hurts, who was on IR, and DAL won 38-21 against the model's PHI by 3.9. PHI at WAS listed him again, and WAS won 27-10 against the model's WAS by 3.3 (Vegas -6). This week the brief's QBs match the news for BAL (Fagnano), SEA (Lock), PHI (Milton) and ARI (Minshew). The model is still 1.4 points on DAL at IND against Vegas -5.5, but I found no news on that game. Far under 20 game…
lessons.test: On past seasons, flag games where a starting QB differed from the one in the model's inputs. Compare the model's margin error in those games with all others. Needs 20+ such games.

lessons.lesson: Most-likely-winner picks have fallen short of the model's own chances.
lessons.evidence: 9 of 17 most-likely-winner picks hit this season, against 12.4 expected, at -5.51 units. Overall winners are 25 of 40 (63%). The sample is under 20 picks, so it moves back to watching.
lessons.test: On past seasons, bucket the model's top win chances (70-79%, 80%+) and compare hit rate with the moneyline-implied chance. Needs 20+ picks per bucket.

news.headline: Boise State QB Madsen out at Colorado State; Cutforth to start
news.detail: ESPN reported Nov 6 that Maddux Madsen (knee) will miss the game, with Max Cutforth making his fourth career start. Madsen is expected back next week against Oregon State.

news.headline: Ole Miss RB Lacy out, nine Rebels ruled out vs Georgia
news.detail: Reports from Nov 5-7 say Ole Miss has nine players out, including running back Kewan Lacy (shoulder). Georgia's running back Chauncey Bowens is probable.

news.headline: Florida turns to Tramell Jones Jr.; Oklahoma fires its OC
news.detail: Florida is expected to start Jones over Aaron Philo (benched after two interceptions vs Georgia), per ESPN on Nov 5. Oklahoma fired offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle this week, and John Mateer is expected to start under interim OC Jason Witten (On3, Nov 6).

news.headline: Miami star WR Toney out vs Notre Dame after ankle surgery
news.detail: Malachi Toney (73 catches, 13 TDs) had tightrope ankle surgery on Nov 5 and is expected to miss the rest of the regular season. Notre Dame is also missing linebacker Drayk Bowen and cornerback DJ McKinney, but cornerback Leonard Moore is expected back.

news.headline: Houston QB Weigman is a full go vs Cincinnati
news.detail: Conner Weigman (ankle/foot) has practiced fully and tight end Patrick Overmyer is also back, per reports from Nov 5-7. Cincinnati expects nose tackle Josh Hough and center Taran Tyo back, though Tyo's clearance was described as unresolved.

news.headline: Air Force QB Evan Medders listed questionable at Army
news.detail: An unofficial injury tracker updated Saturday morning (Nov 7) lists Medders as questionable. This comes from an unofficial source, so treat it with care.

news.headline: New Mexico State short on receivers, no settled QB vs Liberty
news.detail: A New Mexico State fan-site preview from Nov 7 says the Aggies lost receiver T.K. King and tight end Josiah Thomas for the season and have no clear starting quarterback. It also expects a very cold night game.

College.recap: Week 10 has been a coin flip so far: the model picked 6 of 12 winners and went 6-5-1 against the spread. Totals went 5 of 12. Three upsets (Buffalo, Illinois over Nebraska, Florida Atlantic over UTSA) came in games the model had close or leaned the other way. Several games were close or low scoring against the line, like Toledo's 20-17 win over Sacramento State, which beat the spread but not the total.

lessons.lesson: The 'model total 3+ above Vegas means the over hits' pattern does not hold up; the over hit less often than not.
lessons.evidence: Weeks 8-9: over hit in 11 of 29 such games. Week 10 so far: 3 of 6 (James Madison, Ball State and Buffalo went over; New Mexico, Toledo and Ohio did not). Combined 14 of 35 (40%).
lessons.test: On past seasons, group games by model total minus Vegas total (0-3, 3-6, 6+) and check how often the over hits in each group. Need 20+ games per group.

lessons.lesson: Big misses are spread across several causes; efficiency leads less clearly than before.
lessons.evidence: Week 9 reviews, 26 games missed by 8+ points: efficiency first in 7, defensive/return touchdowns 6, turnovers 5, finishing drives 5, nothing stood out 3. Week 8 had efficiency first in 15 of 25. No new reviews this run. Efficiency is measured after the game, so it partly restates the miss.
lessons.test: On past seasons, check whether a team's success rate in prior games predicts the model's error next game. Also compare turnover margin, defensive/return touchdowns and points per trip inside the 40 with long-run averages, to see if misses lean one way or are random.

lessons.lesson: When the model picks a different winner than Vegas, results are mixed to poor.
lessons.evidence: About 4 of 11 right overall. No new disagreements among the 12 Week 10 results; the model and Vegas picked the same side in each. Ole Miss (model 50%, Vegas picks Georgia) is the open case this week. Sample is small.
lessons.test: On past seasons, list games where the model and Vegas disagree on the winner, then compare the model's win rate with Vegas's. Need 20+ games.

lessons.lesson: The 'Best value against the sportsbook' list has been weak.
lessons.evidence: Season: 8 of 22 hit against 11.2 expected, at -6.73 units. The edges are thin (about 51% against 52.4% needed), so the model's own chance is below break-even on all five Week 10 picks. Charlotte +8.5 points against the model's own UAB by 17.8.
lessons.test: On past seasons, bucket the model's spread and total picks by edge size and compare hit rates with the 52.4% break-even. Check that each pick's cover chance matches the model's own margin. Need 20+ games per bucket.

lessons.lesson: Underdog picks have hit a bit less often than the model expected, but long prices have kept units positive.
lessons.evidence: Season: 7 of 22 hit against 8.3 expected, at +0.48 units (was 6 of 21, 7.9 expected, -1.16 units last run). One more hit swung the units a lot, which shows how much luck is in this list.
lessons.test: On past seasons, compare predicted chance with actual win rate for the model's underdog picks, in buckets of model chance (under 35%, 35-45%, 45%+). Need 20+ picks per bucket.

lessons.lesson: The 'Most likely winners' list has landed close to the model's own chances.
lessons.evidence: Season: 17 of 19 hit against 17.0 expected, at -0.30 units. Prices are very short, so one miss costs a lot. Only 19 picks.
lessons.test: On past seasons, bucket the model's top win chances (90%+, 85-90%) and compare with actual win rate and with Vegas's no-vig chance. Need 20+ games per bucket.

lessons.lesson: The model's spread misses are slightly larger than Vegas's over the season.
lessons.evidence: Season (184 games): average spread miss 12.3 points for the model against 11.7 for Vegas, a 0.6 gap unchanged. Winners right in 122 of 184 (66%), spread record 88-89-4. Week 10 so far: 6 of 12 winners and 6-5-1 against the spread.
lessons.test: On past seasons, compare the model's and Vegas's average spread error. Then test whether averaging the model's margin and Vegas's margin beats either alone, and whether the gap changes by week of season.

lessons.lesson: The model does not see starting-quarterback injuries; when a QB is out, its margin runs well above Vegas's.
lessons.evidence: Week 9: Kansas State (starter and backup hurt) was model +9.1 vs Vegas +2.5 and lost 27-24 at Colorado. This week Boise State's Madsen is out (model Boise State by 24.5 vs Vegas 16.5), Florida switches QBs, and Air Force's QB is questionable. One graded game so far; the Boise State result will be the second.
lessons.test: On past seasons, flag games where a team's starting QB was out and compare the model's margin error and the Vegas error in those games with all other games. Need 20+ such games.
